key_insight: TREX automates the entire LLM fine-tuning life cycle by combining a Researcher and an Executor agent with a tree-based exploration strategy to discover, run, and refine training decisions automatically.
problem_solved: Manual LLM training requires repeated, time-consuming cycles of requirement analysis, literature/data search, experimental design, execution, and tuning; TREX addresses the lack of end-to-end automation for that workflow.
method: Two cooperating agents: Researcher (specifies goals, mines literature/data, proposes hypotheses) and Executor (implements experiments, runs code, gathers metrics).
Tree-based exploration over the training design space (datasets, objectives, architectures, hyperparameters) to systematically branch, evaluate, and prune candidate strategies.
Closed-loop orchestration: iterative propose → execute → evaluate → refine, enabling end-to-end automation of dataset preparation, training, evaluation, and tuning.
impact: TREX reduces manual effort and accelerates iterative LLM fine-tuning, improving experiment throughput, reproducibility, and accessibility for AI/ML practitioners.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing Researcher ↔ Executor loop coordinating requirement analysis → design → execution → evaluation.
Tree/search visualization with branches for different datasets/objectives/hyperparameters and pruning based on evaluation metrics.
Lifecycle timeline (requirements, literature/data research, experiment design, training, evaluation, deployment) highlighting automation at each stage.
Metric convergence chart comparing manual workflow vs TREX (fewer iterations, faster improvement) or a dashboard mockup of auto-generated experiment reports.
paper_title: TREX: Automating LLM Fine-tuning via Agent-Driven Tree-based Exploration
paper_authors: Zerun Ma, Guoqiang Wang, Xinchen Xie, Yicheng Chen, He Du
